unit: institution: activity pairs (X30) and pooled evidence per merged activity (X31)
system_prompt: You are a research coder for the Global Government GenAI Observatory (G3O), a public, auditable dataset that measures how government institutions worldwide adopt generative AI. You read two activity records, or a set of quotes about one activity gathered from several sources, about a named institution and answer coding questions about them. Use only what the text says: record what it states explicitly and never infer, guess or use outside knowledge. Give each answer in the form the question asks for and nothing else: for a question with listed answers, choose from those answers only; for an extraction, copy the exact words from the text.

part_prompt.sentence: The text below is only one part of a longer page; the rest of the page is read separately. Answer from this part only.

temporary_answer.label: not covered by this part
temporary_answer.meaning: This part of the page does not deal with the question; another part of the page may.

state.record_value_form: plain-word labels (W7 (ii) b, as W-03 a): activity_type, action_type and source_type as their value's entailment_label (codebook X35 label_rules), not the code; year_announced as the calendar (CE) year in four ASCII digits (X35 label_rules); activity_name, tool_name, contracting_party, developer, page_url and the quotes as stored (not coded values)
state.record_missing_value_form: left out: a record field whose value is not_documented, unknown, not_asked or _NA_ gives no field (as W3-2 a)

questions.instructions: How is the activity in the first record related to the activity in the second record?

criteria.text:
The two activity records describe the same activity: the same action by the same actor on the same tool or instrument. Only records joined by this link are merged.

Rules:
1. Every pair of activity observations is asked, including identical names; candidate pairs pre-filtered deterministically only to skip obviously distinct pairs (different activity_type and tool), never to merge.
2. One activity = one action (deployment, governance instrument, staff training) by one actor concerning one tool or instrument. A named program is one activity; each named component is its own activity, linked to the program as a component of it. Repeated transactions for the same product by the same unit are one activity. A policy and the tools it approves are separate activities, linked by a "governs" relation.
3. One shared relation list serves within-page and cross-page links: same activity, component of program, has component, shared participation, governs, governed by, distinct (`distinct_action`), unresolved, plus not-an-activity within a page.
4. Add "has component" and "governed by".
5. Components stay separate activities; a governing policy is recorded as governing.
6. Store the distinct value with a rule note.

pooled.instruction: The text below is a set of quotes about one activity, gathered from several sources, each with its source type and date. Answer each question about the activity from these quotes only.
pooled.membership: every activity.json question (SPEC R-004: pass 2 = the Group D codes); reported to the integrator for confirmation

state.instruction_placement: a state field with the pooled material; questions stay exactly as signed

quote_fields.name: source_publication_date
quote_fields.value: date: the date the source was published

state.quote_source_type_form: its value's entailment_label (signed label), not the code
state.quote_missing_date_form: left out: a quote with no publication date has no source_publication_date field (as W3-2 a)
state.pool_order: source date, then position on the page (combining convention first_part)
